chunks: As for what 'Ali ibn al-Husayn reported from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn 'Ali, from 'Abd Allah ibn al-Salt, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from 'Abd Allah ibn Sinan — who said:

I said to Abu 'Abd Allah (AS): 'How should I apply the hanoot (camphor)?' He said: 'Place it on his mouth, his ear openings (masami'), and the marks of prostration — on his face, his hands, and his knees.'

The [correct] interpretation of this narration is that we should take his saying 'fi masami'ihi' (in his ear openings) to mean 'upon' — for prepositions can substitute for one another. Allah the Exalted said:
«And I shall surely crucify you upon the trunks of the palm trees»

— by which He meant 'upon the trunks of the palm trees.' We have done this [interpretation] so as to accord with the earlier narrations and to be consistent with what we presented in the commentary on enshrouding (takfin) the deceased in our major book [al-Mabsut], so as not to contradict it.

key_terms.آثَارُ السُّجُودِ: marks of prostration — the seven bodily contact-points used in sajdah: forehead, nose, two palms, two knees, two big toes
key_terms.الْحَنُوطُ: camphor-based aromatic paste applied to the deceased during funeral preparation
key_terms.حُرُوفُ الصِّفَاتِ: prepositions (lit. 'letters of description'), which may substitute for one another in Arabic usage

ai.seo_question: According to Imam al-Sadiq (AS), on which parts of the deceased's body should hanoot (camphor) be applied during funeral preparation?
ai.summary: 'Abd Allah ibn Sinan asked Imam Abu 'Abd Allah al-Sadiq (AS) how to apply the hanoot (camphor paste) to the deceased; the Imam replied that it should be placed on the mouth, the ear openings (masami'), and the seven marks of prostration on the face, hands, and knees. Sheikh al-Tusi appends a linguistic gloss, arguing that the preposition 'fi' (in) in 'fi masami'ihi' must be read as 'ala' (upon), citing Q. 20:71 as a Quranic precedent for prepositional interchange, thereby reconciling this narration with the earlier reports in the chapter.
